name: Royal Holloway, University of London

settingEvidence.evidence: Our Egham campus is one of the most beautiful in the world, with numerous teaching and study spaces, bars and cafés, high-quality accommodation and sports facilities.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK (Home) students starting in 2027/28. Different fees apply to some Foundation Year and accelerated degree courses and to a year spent abroad or working in industry. Fees are reviewed each year and may rise for continuing students.

source.evidence: The tuition fee for students starting their degree in 2027/28 will be £10,050 for that year.

livingCosts.text: Undergraduate halls at Egham cost about £111–£258 a week in 2026/27 (£111.02 is a shared bedroom in Founder's Building; en-suite rooms are mostly £204–£258). Halls such as George Eliot, Gowar and Founder's are on 38-week contracts (September to June). Bills and internet are included; Founder's and Reid are catered (one meal a day plus a £25 weekly allowance).

openDays.text: Next Egham campus open day: Saturday 14 November 2026. Online open days: Wednesday 4 November and Wednesday 9 December 2026. No 2027 dates listed yet.

source.evidence: Our next Open Day will be taking place on Saturday 14 November.

contextual.summary: UK-resident applicants who meet the course entry requirements and Royal Holloway's widening access criteria automatically get a contextual offer of up to 2 A-level grades lower; there is no separate application.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to 2 A-level grades lower than the entry requirements advertised (subject-specific grades and GCSEs are not reduced; not for Integrated Foundation Year courses)

criteria.detail: In Local Authority care for more than 3 months at the time of applying: you automatically get a contextual offer if you meet all the course entry requirements (you may also be eligible for the £3,000-a-year bursary).
Disability or health condition that impacts your daily life (guided by the definitions on the UCAS form, which typically follow the Equality Act 2010).
Mature student (aged 21 or over when the course starts).
In receipt of free school meals.

Attend an 'Aspiring School': the lowest 30% of colleges and lowest 20% of schools on pupils' performance in three academic qualifications (Gov.UK data); Royal Holloway publishes a list. Counts towards the 'meet 2 of these 3' route.
Home postcode in IMD quintile 1 or 2 (English indices of deprivation 2025, deciles 1 to 4). Counts towards the 'meet 2 of these 3' route.
Home postcode in a lower participation in higher education neighbourhood (POLAR4 quintile 1). Counts towards the 'meet 2 of these 3' route.

contextual.rulesText: You must be a UK resident and currently or previously at a UK school or college. Then either (1) you have been in Local Authority care for more than 3 months, or (2) you meet 1 of: disability or health condition, mature student, estranged from parents, refugee or asylum seeker, free school meals, caring responsibilities, or (3) you meet 2 of: attend an Aspiring School, IMD quintile 1/2 postcode, POLAR4 quintile 1 postcode. Nothing extra to do: Royal Holloway uses your UCAS form. minCriteria 2 applies to route (3) only.

source.evidence: You must then meet 1 of the Widening Access criteria, which are listed below:

programmes.name: Summer University - Year 12
programmes.summary: Free two-day residential at Royal Holloway for Year 12 students from widening access backgrounds, with subject insight sessions, social activities and a night in campus accommodation.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students studying A levels (or equivalent) predicted no lower than CCC, with 5 GCSEs at grades 9 to 4 including Maths and English, who do not attend a fee-paying school, have lived in the UK for at least 3 years and meet the widening access criteria (see details). Get your school's permission before applying.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Must be in Year 12; study A levels or equivalent predicted no lower than CCC; have 5 GCSEs at 9 to 4 including Maths and English; not attend a fee-paying school; have lived in the UK for at least three years; AND 'meet this criteria' OR two of these other widening access criteria: in or has been in Local Authority care; both parents/guardians have no experience of UK higher education; eligible for free school meals, pupil premium or other additional funding; disability or health condition affecting daily life; home postcode in IMD Q1/2 or POLAR4 Q1; Black or Mixed Black heritage; care responsibilities; armed forces family; refugee or asylum seeker who has lived in the UK for at least 3 years; estranged from parents/carers.
benefits: Free: accommodation, all food and drink, and all resources and academic activities are covered
Subject insight sessions (seminars and lectures) led by staff and current student ambassadors
Stay in your own en-suite student room on campus and experience university life
Information sessions on your next steps after school or college
programmes.subjects: Subject insight sessions matched to the subjects you study (subjects not guaranteed)

programmes.name: Royal Holloway Link
programmes.summary: Free series of four sessions for Year 13 students (mostly online, some on campus) with advice from student ambassadors on study skills, applying through UCAS, finance and accommodation.
programmes.whoCanApply: All Year 13 students are welcome (UK residents studying A levels or equivalent predicted no lower than CCC, with 5 GCSEs at 9 to 4), with priority for students who meet widening access criteria.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Priority (not a requirement) goes to students who: have a disability or health condition; live in a POLAR4 Q1 or IMD deciles 1 to 4 postcode; are or will be mature students; receive free school meals; attend a Widening Access partner school; are or have been in local authority care; are young carers or have caring responsibilities; are estranged from both parents/carers; or are refugees or asylum seekers.
benefits: Study and revision skills for Year 13 and higher education
Advice on applying to higher education (personal statement, finance, accommodation)
Meet students from other schools and current Royal Holloway students
programmes.cost: Free (travel to the on-campus sessions is not reimbursed)
programmes.subjects: All subjects (study skills and university applications)

runs.text: Four sessions from Saturday 31 October 2026 to Saturday 20 February 2027 (2026/27 round)

opens.text: 2026/27 applications are closed; 2027/28 opening date not published

source.evidence: Our contextual offer is a reduction of the equivalent of up to 2 A-Level grades lower* compared to the original entry requirements advertised on our website and undergraduate prospectus.

alternativeOffers.conditions: Taking an Extended Project Qualification (EPQ) alongside your A-levels will be taken into consideration and could result in lower entry requirements in your offer; no fixed reduction is published (the page's example is an offer of BBB with B in the EPQ instead of ABB).
